artists.biography: Ride were a British shoegazing band that formed in 1988 in Oxford, England, consisting of Andy Bell, Mark Gardener, Laurence "Loz" Colbert, and Steve Queralt. The band were initially part of the "shoegazing" scene that emerged in England during the early 1990s. Following the break-up of the band in 1996, members moved on to various other projects, most notably Bell who became the bassist for Oasis. In 2001, the band members were briefly reunited for a one-off performance for a television show. Their debut album 'Nowhere' has been named one of the greatest albums of the shoegazing genre, Nowhere was voted number 74 on Pitchfork Media's list of the Top 100 Albums of the 1990s, and closing track "Vapour Trail" was voted at number 145 on Pitchfork's Top 200 Tracks of the 90s. The album is also included in the book '1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die'.

perplexity.description:
OX4: The Best of Ride is a compilation album by British alternative rock band Ride, released in 2001 by Ignition Records. The collection surveys the band's career, drawing from their output across the 1990s when they were prominent figures in the shoegaze and alternative rock movements. As a retrospective, the album captures Ride's evolution from their early shoegaze-influenced work through their later, more guitar-driven alternative rock sound.

The compilation serves as an accessible entry point to Ride's discography, presenting key tracks that defined their commercial and critical presence during the 1990s. The band's signature approach—characterized by layered guitars, melodic sensibilities, and atmospheric production—is well-represented across the selection. OX4 reflects Ride's position within the broader alternative rock landscape of their era, showcasing why they maintained a dedicated following despite the shifting musical trends of the decade.

The album's reception as a retrospective was generally positive within fan circles and among those revisiting the band's catalog. Its release in 2001 came during a period when 1990s alternative rock was being reassessed and recontextualized, making it a timely documentation of Ride's contributions to the genre. The compilation has since been reissued on vinyl, indicating sustained interest in the band's legacy among collectors and new listeners discovering their work.
